circle.definition: A round, flat shape whose boundary stays the same distance from its center.
circle.exampleUsage: Draw a circle around the correct answer.

square.definition: A flat shape with four equal sides and four right angles.
square.exampleUsage: The tile is a square with equal sides.

triangle.definition: A flat shape with three straight sides and three corners.
triangle.exampleUsage: The sign has the shape of a triangle.

rectangle.definition: A flat shape with four straight sides and four right angles.
rectangle.exampleUsage: Draw a rectangle around the address.

oval.definition: A rounded, flat shape that is longer in one direction.
oval.exampleUsage: The mirror has an oval frame.

diamond.definition: A four-sided shape with equal sides, usually shown resting on one corner.
diamond.exampleUsage: The pattern has a diamond in the center.

pentagon.definition: A flat shape with five straight sides and five corners.
pentagon.exampleUsage: Draw a pentagon with five sides.

hexagon.definition: A flat shape with six straight sides and six corners.
hexagon.exampleUsage: Each cell has the shape of a hexagon.

octagon.definition: A flat shape with eight straight sides and eight corners.
octagon.exampleUsage: The stop sign is an octagon.

star.definition: A flat shape with points extending outward from its center.
star.exampleUsage: Place a star beside your favorite design.

sphere.definition: A round solid whose surface stays the same distance from its center.
sphere.exampleUsage: The model globe is a sphere.

cube.definition: A solid shape with six equal square faces.
cube.exampleUsage: Each face of the cube is the same size.

cylinder.definition: A solid with two equal, parallel circular ends joined by a curved surface.
cylinder.exampleUsage: The can has the shape of a cylinder.

cone.definition: A solid with a circular base that narrows to one point.
cone.exampleUsage: The party hat has the shape of a cone.

pyramid.definition: A solid with a polygon base and triangular faces meeting at one point.
pyramid.exampleUsage: The paper pyramid has a pointed top.

prism.definition: A solid with two matching, parallel polygon bases joined by flat faces.
prism.exampleUsage: The package has the shape of a triangular prism.

cuboid.definition: A solid shape with six rectangular faces and eight corners.
cuboid.exampleUsage: The shipping box is a cuboid.

hemisphere.definition: One half of a solid ball, divided through its center.
hemisphere.exampleUsage: The bowl is shaped like a hemisphere.

torus.definition: A ring-shaped solid or surface with a hole through the middle.
torus.exampleUsage: The model torus looks like a doughnut.

tetrahedron.definition: A solid shape with four triangular faces and four corners.
tetrahedron.exampleUsage: The tetrahedron has four triangular faces.

line.definition: A straight path that extends endlessly in both directions in geometry.
line.exampleUsage: Mark two points on the line.

curve.definition: A line or boundary that bends rather than staying straight.
curve.exampleUsage: Follow the curve along the edge of the drawing.

straight.definition: Continuing in one direction without bending or turning.
straight.exampleUsage: Use a ruler to draw a straight mark.

zigzag.definition: A path or pattern that repeatedly changes direction at sharp angles.
zigzag.exampleUsage: The border has a zigzag pattern.

spiral.definition: A curve that winds around a centre while moving inward or outward.
spiral.exampleUsage: Draw a spiral from the center outward.

right-angle.definition: An angle measuring exactly ninety degrees, like the corner of a sheet of paper.
right-angle.exampleUsage: The corner forms a right angle.

acute-angle.definition: An angle measuring more than zero degrees but less than ninety degrees.
acute-angle.exampleUsage: The narrow corner forms an acute angle.

obtuse-angle.definition: An angle measuring more than ninety degrees but less than one hundred eighty degrees.
obtuse-angle.exampleUsage: The open door forms an obtuse angle with the wall.

parallel.definition: Describes straight lines in the same plane that never meet.

perpendicular.definition: Describes lines or surfaces that meet at a ninety-degree angle.
perpendicular.exampleUsage: The vertical mark is perpendicular to the base.

area.definition: The amount of space inside a flat shape, measured in square units.
area.exampleUsage: Measure the area of the floor before buying tiles.

perimeter.definition: The total distance around the outside boundary of a flat shape.
perimeter.exampleUsage: Measure the perimeter before fitting the border.

volume.definition: The amount of space a solid occupies, measured in cubic units.
volume.exampleUsage: The box has a volume of eight cubic meters.

radius.definition: The distance from the center of a circle to its boundary.
radius.exampleUsage: The wheel has a radius of thirty centimeters.

diameter.definition: The distance across a circle through its center, from one boundary point to another.
diameter.exampleUsage: Measure the diameter across the middle of the lid.

circumference.definition: The distance around the boundary of a circle.
circumference.exampleUsage: Wrap a tape around the wheel to measure its circumference.

diagonal.definition: A line joining two corners of a polygon that are not next to each other.
diagonal.exampleUsage: Draw a diagonal across the rectangle.

symmetry.definition: The property of matching parts after a reflection, rotation, or other transformation.
symmetry.exampleUsage: The folded design has reflection symmetry.

vertex.definition: A point where sides or edges of a geometric shape meet.
vertex.exampleUsage: Mark the vertex at the top of the shape.

edge.definition: A boundary of a flat shape, or a line where two solid faces meet.
edge.exampleUsage: Run your finger along one edge of the box.

repeat.definition: To do, say, or show the same thing again.
repeat.exampleUsage: Repeat the design across the page.

sequence.definition: An arrangement of items that follow one another in a particular order.
sequence.exampleUsage: Continue the sequence with the next shape.

pattern.definition: An arrangement of shapes, colors, or objects that follows a recognizable rule.
pattern.exampleUsage: The fabric has a repeating pattern.

tessellation.definition: An arrangement of flat shapes covering a surface without gaps or overlaps.
tessellation.exampleUsage: The floor tiles form a tessellation.

fractal.definition: A geometric pattern with similar features appearing at increasingly small scales.
fractal.exampleUsage: The computer displays a detailed fractal.

grid.definition: A network of crossing lines used to divide a surface into regular spaces.
grid.exampleUsage: Use the grid to position each icon.

array.definition: An ordered arrangement of objects, often in rows and columns.
array.exampleUsage: Arrange the dots in a rectangular array.

matrix.definition: A rectangular arrangement of numbers or expressions in rows and columns.
matrix.exampleUsage: Enter the values into the matrix.

mosaic.definition: A picture or design made from small pieces placed together.
mosaic.exampleUsage: The wall has a colorful mosaic.

kaleidoscope.definition: A viewing tube with mirrors that produce changing patterns from colored pieces.
kaleidoscope.exampleUsage: Turn the kaleidoscope to change the design.
